motions.item_title: Approve the minutes of April 14, 2026, Planning Commission meeting. Commissioner Strong seconde…
motions.motion: Commissioner Allen moved to approve the minutes of April 14, 2026, Planning Commission meeting. Commissioner Strong seconded the motion.
motions.headline: April 14 minutes approved
motions.summary: The commission approved the minutes of its April 14 meeting.
motions.impact: Housekeeping for the record: it makes the account of that meeting official. Nothing here reaches your street.

motions.item_title: Recommend approval to the City Council of Item 7.A., Wildlife Urban Interface Code Amendment, w…
motions.motion: Commissioner Allen moved to recommend approval to the City Council of Item 7.A., Wildlife Urban Interface Code Amendment, with the following changes: 1. Remove the language of rear setback and have it apply to the setback that's next to the WUI boundary. 2. That the code also be applied to primary and accessory structures. Commissioner Free seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Setback rules along the wildlife interface boundary
motions.summary: The commission backed a code change moving the setback from the rear lot line to the wildlife urban interface boundary, and applying it to homes and outbuildings.
motions.impact: Owners whose lots touch that boundary would measure the setback from the boundary, not the back property line, and outbuildings would count too. The council has the final say.

motions.item_title: Table Item 7.B., EMMC Chapter 16.15 – Concept Plans, until the May 12, 2026 Planning Commission…
motions.motion: Commissioner Strong moved to table Item 7.B., EMMC Chapter 16.15 – Concept Plans, until the May 12, 2026 Planning Commission meeting. Commissioner Allen seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Concept plan rules put off to May
motions.summary: The commission delayed a decision on the city's concept plan rules until its May 12 meeting.
motions.impact: The existing rules stay in place until then. Only people filing concept plans have a reason to follow this one.

motions.item_title: Recommend approval to the City Council of Item 7.C., Preliminary Plat – Spring Run Plaza, with…
motions.motion: Commissioner Hess moved to recommend approval to the City Council of Item 7.C., Preliminary Plat – Spring Run Plaza, with the following conditions: 1. The Master Development Agreement is approved and executed. 2. The right turn lane be extended to the service drive. Commissioner Allen seconded the motion.
motions.headline: First-stage plat for Spring Run Plaza
motions.summary: Backing the site's lot layout, the commission sent the Spring Run Plaza preliminary plat to the council, conditioned on a signed agreement and the extended turn lane.
motions.impact: This is the lot layout step, and it holds until the council acts and the agreement is signed. Builders on that site are watching; nobody else needs to.

motions.item_title: Recommend approval to the City Council of Item 7.D., Spring Run Plaza Master Development Agreem…
motions.motion: Commissioner Hess moved to recommend approval to the City Council of Item 7.D., Spring Run Plaza Master Development Agreement, with the recommendation that the right turn lane be extended to the service drive. Commissioner Strong seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Spring Run Plaza development deal sent to council
motions.summary: The commission recommended the Spring Run Plaza master development agreement, asking that the right turn lane be extended to the service drive.
motions.impact: Nothing is built on this yet: the council votes later. Neighbors of the site and drivers turning in are the ones who would notice, with a longer turn lane feeding the plaza's service drive.
